newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Optus says sorts out telephony problems.
newsitem.headline: Optus says sorts out telephony problems.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Wednesday that it had sorted out many of the technology related problems with the delivery of local telephony services over its fibre optic network.

"As far as the technology is concerned we are very pleased with the progress we have made in the last couple of months as far as far as establishing the product and now we have a commercially viable product," chief operating officer Phil Jacobs told reporters.
Optus' local telephony service has faced technology-related problems since its launch a year ago to much fanfare.
"The demand for the product continues to be extremely strong, well outstripping our ability to deliver," Jacobs said.
However, Jacobs said Optus does not plan a major relaunch of the service, because it wanted to meet the current level of demand.
"Right now the demand is significant without a major marketing effort and we want to make sure that this technology does grow in terms of scale and load," Jacobs said.
Jacobs said he could not provide details of local telephony customer numbers, but added the group may release numbers in the near future.
